job.title: Account Executive
job.description: iHeartMedia Markets Current employees and contingent workers click here to apply and search by the Job Posting Title. The audio revolution is here – and iHeart is leading it! iHeartMedia, the number one audio company in America , reaches 90% of Americans every month -- a monthly audience that’s twice the size of any other audio company – almost three times the size of the largest TV network – and almost 4 times the size of the largest ad-supported music streaming service. And we were just recognized as one of the Top Media Sales Organizations by The Myers Report! In fact, iHeart has: More #1 rated markets than the next two largest radio companies combined; We’re the largest podcast publisher , with more monthly downloads than the second- and third-largest podcast publishers combined. Podcasting, the fastest-growing new media, today has more monthly users than streaming music services or Netflix; iHeart is the home of many of the country’s most popular and trusted on-air personalities and podcast influencers , who build important connections with hundreds of communities across America; We create and produce some of the most popular and well-known branded live music events in America, including the iHeartRadio Music Festival, the iHeartRadio Music Awards, the iHeartCountry Festival, iHeartRadio Fiesta Latina and the iHeartRadio Jingle Ball Tour; iHeartRadio is the #1 streaming radio digital service in America; Our social media footprint is 7 times larger than the next largest audio service; and We have the only complete audio ad technology stack in the industry for all forms of audio , from on demand to broadcast radio, digital streaming radio and podcasting, which bring data, targeting and attribution to all forms of audio at an unparalleled scale. As a result, we’re able to combine our strong leadership position in audience reach, usage and ad tech with powerful tools and insights for our sales organizations to help them build success for their clients at a more efficient cost than any other option. Because we reach almost every community in America, we’re committed to providing a range of programming that reflects the diversity of the many communities we serve – and our company reflects that same kind of diversity. Our company values stress collaboration, curiosity, welcoming dissent, accepting mistakes in the pursuit of new ideas, and respect for everyone. Only one company in America has the #1 position in everything audio: iHeartMedia! If you’re excited about this role but don’t feel your experience aligns perfectly with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. At iHeartMedia we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace and are looking for teammates passionate about what we do! What We Need: Looking for a new challenge? Join us as an Account Executive and leverage your proven goal-driven mindset, fast-paced work ethic, and exceptional client service skills. The ideal candidate is ready to hit the ground running and will successfully take advantage of all iHeart’s platforms to exceed their clients’ expectations. What You'll Do: As an Account Executive at iHeart, you'll learn the ins and outs of our Broadcast + Digital Marketing Products, identify and develop new business opportunities through in-person meetings with clients and research, consistent daily cold-calling, and cultivate existing business using our full suite of products. You will collaborate with internal partners to drive revenue, create effective marketing campaigns, and use your storytelling skills to deliver compelling sales presentations fueled by data to best meet your clients’ expectations. What You'll Need: You should be self-motivated (a very “go-getter” attitude!), have excellent relationship-building and problem-solving skills, and communicate persuasively. When people describe you, goal-oriented, expert negotiator and proactive should be at the top of the list. You should be able to plan and multi-task in a fast-paced environment . Comfortable with cold-calling and initiating outreach to prospective clients as part of lead generation efforts. A valid driver's license, auto insurance, and a High School Diploma (College Degree preferred) are required. You should also be skilled in Salesforce, Microsoft Office and social networking platforms. Strong problem-solving skills; by exercising these skills, you help business grow to the fullest potential. Digital/Media Sales experience are a plus but not required. The natural ability to organize and prioritize day-to-day depending on where the biggest priorities may be Additional nice-to-haves include experience managing complex, multi-platform campaigns , analytics experience, iHeart and/or audio advertising background, and are well-connected in the market. What you’ll get You'll have the opportunity for uncapped commission , and the ability to grow business across all categories on a local, regional, and national level no matter where you live A 7-week onboarding program to immerse you in the suite of tools and products available to you The potential to be recognized in our annual iHeartMedia CEO’s Club a nd iHeartMedia President’s Club programs Access to competitive benefits including paid vacation and sick time , paid company holidays , a Spirit day to encourage the opportunity to more easily volunteer in their communities, company-paid mental health and financial education resources, 401(k) matching , learning and development resources, and career navigation support. Access to additional perks include pet (they’re part of the family!), disaster , and legal insurance, student loan refinancing , and discounts on merchandise, tickets to events, and more. The support of fellow team members invested in your success. Envision your first 30 days Week 1: Complete our onboarding journey for a deep understanding of our company, job-specific trainings and spend time with your team. Week 2: Spend more time with your manager to ensure you are aligned on work and communication styles, priorities, and any other expectations. Week 3: Start “owning” your role and leaning into the real day-to-day, of course with your manager’s support and advocacy! The same program is released in podcast form for on-demand listening. The Associate Producer plays an important role in the preparation of materials and content research for the daily program, in addition to being a vital part of the program during its daily live broadcast creation. What You'll Do: The individual who fills this role is expected to know and provide the following: An ongoing knowledge of the audience and their expectations for both information and entertainment while listening / viewing the program. An excellent knowledge of current events in U.S. and world politics, news events across the U.S. and world. The ability to determine the most impactful words shared from individuals who are a part of news stories or those covering them, elected politicians, appointed government officials, commentators appearing in television and radio programs, podcasts and speaking events and edit them to be made ready for consideration to be aired within the radio program. The ability to work quickly to find and obtain audio originating from events happening in real-time during the programs’ broadcasts and make them available ASAP for the hosts consideration. The ability to transcribe the words selected for possible airing and providing a proper context who and where the words originated from in summary form for the hosts to consider using and the other producers of the program to work alongside of. An ability to screen phone calls from listeners of the show in such a way to determine the most entertaining calls that benefit the programs’ listening experience, and by supporting the hosts’ ability to further explore a topic from a different perspective or angle. This work requires a discerning ear and thought process, looking for only specific types of callers that are articulate, use good word economy and can be entertaining. This aspect of the position happens concurrently with listening to the program and maintaining a knowledge of the current conversations and what the hosts are saying on-air, requiring focus and concentration during the three hours of each program. An interest and ability to schedule guests for the program, coordinating their appearance with specific times and technical logistics. Maintain a general knowledge of the Executive Producer role of the program, so as to assume those responsibilities 20+ times per year while also maintaining current duties. Maintain a productive, professional relationship with the hosts, taking into account their feedback of the audio offerings provided to them in the form of audio soundbites prepared in advance, guest booking preferences and prior approvals, listener call and listener audio feedback via Talkback technology and other forms of communication to be incorporated into the program. Obtain and become familiar with the workflow of the program’s Board Operator role and general responsibilities for the rare occasions when the program can rely on you to originate the sound of the program when primary and secondary options are not available. Maintain a trusting relationship with the hosts of the program, maintaining discretion for all conversations and actions within the studio environment and in separate communications before and after the program. Receive feedback from the hosts in a manner to help them maximize their listener relationships and audience size potential. Being open to selectively being referred to in programming conversations, and in rare cases, being called upon to speak on-air when the hosts find the conversation input appropriate. Recognizing that the program is opinion and commentary based, and the hosts are required to offer their opinions and welcome the opinions of others including guests and listeners. The opinions expressed may not be the same as your own, but your professionalism dictates allowing those opinions to be shared at the sole discretion of the hosts. This is a full-time position requiring a physical presence in the studio and control room environment daily. It is not a remote working position. The position requires a knowledge of the broadcast clock of the program and being mindful at all times to be physically and mentally present during the same hours as the program originates, as well as the necessary hours beforehand and afterwards to prepare for the present program and future programs. Only one company in America has the #1 position in everything audio: iHeartMedia! If you’re excited about this role but don’t feel your experience aligns perfectly with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. At iHeartMedia we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace and are looking for teammates passionate about what we do! What We Need: Looking for a new challenge? Join us as an Account Executive and leverage your proven goal-driven mindset, fast-paced work ethic, and exceptional client service skills. The ideal candidate is ready to hit the ground running and will successfully take advantage of all iHeart’s platforms to exceed their clients’ expectations. What You'll Do: As an Account Executive at iHeart, you'll learn the ins and outs of our Broadcast + Digital Marketing Products, identify and develop new business opportunities through in-person meetings with clients and research, consistent daily cold-calling, and cultivate existing business using our full suite of products. You will collaborate with internal partners to drive revenue, create effective marketing campaigns, and use your storytelling skills to deliver compelling sales presentations fueled by data to best meet your clients’ expectations. What You'll Need: You should be self-motivated (a very “go-getter” attitude!), have excellent relationship-building and problem-solving skills, and communicate persuasively. When people describe you, goal-oriented, expert negotiator and proactive should be at the top of the list. You should be able to plan and multi-task in a fast-paced environment . Comfortable with cold-calling and initiating outreach to prospective clients as part of lead generation efforts. A valid driver's license, auto insurance, and a High School Diploma (College Degree preferred) are required. You should also be skilled in Salesforce, Microsoft Office and social networking platforms. Strong problem-solving skills; by exercising these skills, you help business grow to the fullest potential. Digital/Media Sales experience are a plus but not required. The natural ability to organize and prioritize day-to-day depending on where the biggest priorities may be Additional nice-to-haves include experience managing complex, multi-platform campaigns , analytics experience, iHeart and/or audio advertising background, and are well-connected in the market. What you’ll get You'll have the opportunity for uncapped commission , and the ability to grow business across all categories on a local, regional, and national level no matter where you live A 7-week onboarding program to immerse you in the suite of tools and products available to you The potential to be recognized in our annual iHeartMedia CEO’s Club a nd iHeartMedia President’s Club programs Access to competitive benefits including paid vacation and sick time , paid company holidays , a Spirit day to encourage the opportunity to more easily volunteer in their communities, company-paid mental health and financial education resources, 401(k) matching , learning and development resources, and career navigation support. Access to additional perks include pet (they’re part of the family!), disaster , and legal insurance, student loan refinancing , and discounts on merchandise, tickets to events, and more. The support of fellow team members invested in your success. Envision your first 30 days Week 1: Complete our onboarding journey for a deep understanding of our company, job-specific trainings and spend time with your team. Week 2: Spend more time with your manager to ensure you are aligned on work and communication styles, priorities, and any other expectations. Week 3: Start “owning” your role and leaning into the real day-to-day, of course with your manager’s support and advocacy! Week 4: Prioritize a 30-day check-in to see what else you might need to be most successful in your new role. Interested in learning more about iHeart and our platforms? Visit us at www.iHeartMedia.com to learn more about our company, www.iHeartRadio.com to access all your favorite music, radio, and podcasts, and download the free iHeartRadio app! job.title: Account Executive (Local Ad Sales), The California Post
job.description: Job Description : California Post is a brand-new digital-first news organization backed by the trusted legacy of the New York Post. Our mission is to deliver breaking news, compelling storytelling, and innovative content to readers across the West Coast. This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast-growing team, shape the future of a newsroom, and help advertisers connect with a highly engaged audience. We are looking for a hungry, results-driven local Ad Sales Account Executive to join our Los Angeles team. This individual contributor role will be responsible for driving new business, managing client relationships, and delivering revenue growth for California Post , with a strong focus on local and regional advertisers. The ideal candidate has a proven track record in media sales, deep local market knowledge, and understands how to prospect, negotiate, and close deals in a competitive marketplace. Responsibilities: Develop and execute a sales strategy to drive revenue growth across digital advertising, sponsorships, and brand partnerships, with an emphasis on local and regional accounts. Identify, prospect, and secure new clients across key local verticals, including Tier 2 automotive, casinos and gaming, real estate, hospitals and healthcare systems, legal services, and other local service-based businesses. Build and maintain strong relationships with local advertisers, agencies, and key regional stakeholders. Collaborate with internal teams, including marketing and editorial, to craft integrated, custom advertising solutions tailored to local market needs. Manage the full sales cycle, including prospecting, RFP responses, contract negotiations, and post-sale account management. Maintain accurate sales forecasts, pipelines, and CRM data. Stay up to date on industry trends, competitors, and emerging opportunities to effectively advise clients and position California Post as a trusted local media partner. Requirements: Minimum of 5 years of advertising sales experience, preferably within media or digital news organizations. Demonstrated success selling to local or regional advertisers, ideally across verticals such as automotive, gaming, real estate, healthcare, or professional services. Proven ability to prospect, close deals, and consistently exceed revenue targets. Strong network of media and advertising contacts in the Los Angeles market. Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills. Self-motivated, goal-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. Ability to manage multiple clients and projects simultaneously with strong attention to detail. Ability and willingness to travel as needed. Note: This role is primarily based in our Los Angeles office. Occasional remote work may be permitted, with the expectation of on-site presence for core team collaboration and client-facing activities, excluding external sales meetings or required travel. Compensation : $100,000 - $125,000 Base + commission/sales bonus plan. A final decision on the successful candidate's starting salary will be based on a number of factors, including but not limited to competitive market practice, internal equity, experience, tenure, and essential skills. At The New York Post Media Group we recognize that attracting the best talent is key to our strategy and success as a company. As a result, our ranges reflect our good faith estimate to pay fairly as to what our ideal candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on the selected candidate's experience, industry knowledge, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the interview process. In addition to compensation, the company provides eligible employees a comprehensive and highly competitive benefits package, with a variety of physical health, retirement and savings, caregiving, emotional wellbeing, transportation, and other benefits, including “elective” benefits employees may select to best fit the needs and personal situations of our diverse workforce. Equal Opportunity Employer All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other protected characteristic. EEO/Disabled/Vets Reasonable Accommodation We are committed to providing reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application and/or interview process. If you need assistance or accommodation in completing your application or participating in an interview due to a disability, email us at humanresources@newscorp.com . Please put "Reasonable Accommodation" in the subject line and provide a brief description of the type of assistance you need. This inbox will not be monitored for application status updates. Please refer to the privacy notice at the bottom of this page for submitting any data access, deletion, or other data subject rights requests, where permitted under your local laws and regulations. Base Pay Range: $100,000 - $125,000 + Commission/Sales Bonus We’re committed to offering competitive and flexible compensation to attract top talent. This pay range reflects our good faith estimate for the role and may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, and other relevant factors. For bonus-eligible roles, targets are determined based on multiple considerations, including market benchmarks and individual contributions. For benefits-eligible roles, we offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package covering health, retirement, wellbeing, and more, along with optional benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees.

job.title: Associate Commerce Editor
job.description: Job Description : About The Post: The New York Post delivers the best in news, sports, entertainment, pop culture and shopping, with wit, irreverence and authority across print, digital, video, audio, app and commerce. The Role: We’re hiring an Associate Commerce Editor for the revenue-generating commerce team. This is not a business reporting role. In this dynamic, expanded position, you will balance daily writing with foundational editing responsibilities, serving as a critical bridge between our reporting and editing desks. You will be responsible for writing a minimum of two short-form deal stories per day, continuing to publish fast, useful shopping stories that drive revenue and taking ownership of editing daily deals, updating evergreen posts and stepping up to manage larger packages when needed. This role is ideal for a prolific commerce reporter ready to hone their editorial judgment, refine their packaging skills and take on emerging leadership responsibilities across the New York Post Digital Network. What You’ll Do: ● Write a baseline of 2–3 commerce stories per shift (deals, explainers, how-tos and buyer’s guides) that drive conversions, ensuring consistent daily revenue-generating output. ● Edit 15+ fast-turn deals and standard shopping content daily from reporters. Move copy from draft to live with speed, ensuring clean formatting, airtight affiliate linking and FTC compliance. ● Take point on executing sponsored content and flat-fee product placements, seamlessly weaving revenue-driven partnerships into daily coverage while maintaining reader trust and the iconic Post voice. ● Step in to report, write or co-edit larger, high-priority features and tentpole packages (Prime Day, Black Friday, Cyber Week) as assigned by leadership. ● Share ownership of the evergreen strategy. Audit and update top-performing posts for price, stock and SEO/AEO/GEO optimization to maximize long-tail revenue. ● Write sharp, on-brand headlines (providing 3-5 variants for testing). Begin providing actionable, constructive feedback to reporters to maintain voice and standards. ● Monitor performance dashboards to iterate headlines, framing and placement. Pitch high-intent stories based on search data, real-time signals and competitor coverage. How We Measure Success: ● Output Balance: Consistent daily writing output (2–3 stories) combined with reliable, rapid editing of assigned copy and on-time handoffs. ● Quality & Accuracy: Clean copy (both written and edited), rigorous fact-checking, zero avoidable corrections and strict link hygiene. ● Impact: Measurable lift in CTR, conversion rates, revenue per session and search visibility for both authored and edited pieces. ● Ownership: Demonstrated progress in editorial decision-making, proactive pitching and the ability to seamlessly pivot between writing and editing mindsets. What You’ll Bring: ● Professional experience commensurate with an associate-level role in features, news or commerce writing, backed by a portfolio of strong clips and early experience (or a demonstrated aptitude) for editing. ● Obsession with the commerce landscape, reader value and producing service-oriented content with a commercial focus. ● Command of the iconic NY Post voice and a proven track record of writing crisp, authoritative headlines. ● Working knowledge of SEO, AEO and GEO, plus social media best practices. ● Comfort reading dashboards (Search Console, GA4, Looker or similar) and using data to pivot quickly to trends or live news without losing accuracy. ● CMS fluency and sharp attention to detail, including mastery of AP style and FTC-compliant disclosures. ● A collaborative, growth-oriented mindset – highly organized, adaptable and ready to take on coaching responsibilities. Nice to Have ● Hands-on familiarity with affiliate dashboards and networks (Amazon Associates, Skimlinks or similar), project management platforms and SEO tools. ● Experience jumping between categories and services that help shoppers protect value. ● Deeper understanding of AEO, GEO and AI overviews. ● Newsletter experience. Note: The New York Post adheres to an on-site work model. This role will be expected to report into the office 5 days per week. job.title: Design Editor
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 225 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. The New York Post is looking for a creative, versatile Design Editor (Tuesday - Saturday, 11am-7pm) to join our fast-paced newsroom. If you have a passion for bold visuals, a digital-first mindset, and the skills to turn ideas into eye-catching designs, this role is for you. As a key member of our Design Team, you'll help bring stories to life across digital and social platforms, as well as print. Responsibilities: Design compelling digital visuals including interactive infographics, illustrations, editorial print features, animations for online and social, composites and maps. Stay ahead of design trends, tools, and techniques to keep our visuals fresh, relevant and competitive. Collaborate with the Lead Design Editor and Sr. Design Editors to develop innovative graphic concepts that align with the Post’s bold brand identity. Work closely with editorial teams to integrate text and visuals seamlessly, enhancing storytelling whether digitally or in print. Generate fresh ideas for visual storytelling, with a strong focus on engaging digital content. Prioritize multiple projects efficiently in a deadline-driven environment. Requirements: Strong proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects) and design tools such as Flourish and MapCreator. A digital-first approach with ability to create designs for web, mobile, and social platforms; Solid foundation in print design techniques is also necessary. Exceptional sense of typography, layout, and visual and information hierarchy. Create charts and visualizations from complex datasets such as financial reports, press releases etc and distill information for general audiences. Ability to think creatively and strategically under tight deadlines. Passion for news, sports, viral content, pop culture, and emerging digital trends. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a proactive approach to problem-solving. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. A portfolio showcasing a range of design work, especially digital projects. Willingness to work on weekends and holidays as needed. Basic coding knowledge (HTML, CSS, JAVA) ​ Note: The New York Post adheres to an on-site work model. This role will be expected to report into the office 5 days per week. job.title: Editorial Page Assistant Editor, New York Post
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post delivers the best in News, Sports, Entertainment and Pop Culture with wit, irreverence, and authority. Over the past 224 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. The Post’s Editorial Page is where bold ideas meet razor-sharp commentary. As one of the country’s most recognized opinion sections, our team tackles the most pressing local, national, and global issues — delivering sharp, fearless takes in the distinct voice that defines the Post. From holding public officials accountable to weighing in on global conflicts, we cut through the noise with clarity, wit, and purpose. We’re looking for a nimble, thoughtful, and fast-moving Editorial Page Assistant Editor to join our Opinion team. This writer will contribute impactful editorials daily — helping shape the voice of our institutional stance — while also crafting occasional bylined opinion columns. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of the Post’s signature tone: smart, punchy, skeptical of orthodoxy, and unafraid to challenge both sides of the aisle. This role is key to helping our readers make sense of a fast-changing world and will contribute to both our print and digital platforms. Responsibilities: Write timely, engaging, and factually sound unsigned editorials under tight deadlines, aligned with the Post’s voice and editorial stance Occasionally contribute bylined opinion columns on topics of expertise or general interest As our video products develop, contribute on-camera opinion on topics of expertise or general interest Pitch compelling editorial ideas that respond to breaking news or trends in politics, policy, and culture Collaborate closely with the editorial team to shape daily and long-term coverage priorities Monitor current events across a wide range of topics including New York City and state politics, national affairs, foreign policy and broader cultural issues Join in team preparation of copy for both digital publication (using WordPress and other CMS tools) and print. Help amplify opinion content’s reach (including via social media) with sharp headlines and an eye toward engagement Represent the editorial board externally as needed, including occasional interviews, panels, or media appearances Requirements: At least 3 years of experience in political commentary, editorial writing, or a related field Deep understanding of New York politics and national political dynamics Exceptional writing skills: clear, direct, and persuasive prose under deadline Strong editorial judgment and a keen news sense Comfort with delivering on-camera content, preferably non-teleprompter Comfort with WordPress or similar content management systems Familiarity with SEO best practices and social media strategy A sharp eye for narrative, logic, and tone — especially attuned to the Post’s unique voice Ability to work independently while thriving in a collaborative, high-paced newsroom environment Note: This role will be expected to report on-site 5 days per week. job.title: Lifestyle Trending News Editor
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post delivers news, sports, pop culture and entertainment with unmatched speed, attitude and authority, reaching more than 90 million unique viewers each month. With a 225 year legacy and a fast moving digital first newsroom, the Post operates across print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce, and continues to define the city’s most talked about stories. We are seeking an experienced and audience driven Lifestyle Trending News Editor (Tuesday-Saturday) to direct our daily lifestyle news content — working across verticals including sex & relationships, fashion, real estate, parenting, travel, food & drink, science & technology and general interest. The successful candidate will be audience and SEO obsessed, have an innate ability to identify the topics everyone wants to read and talk about, and have proven experience in using data and insights platforms to maximize traffic. They will have proven skills at crafting audience and editorial strategy, be obsessed with setting the lifestyle news agenda, driving traffic across multiple sources, and know how to write a sparkling headline that everyone wants to click on. The candidate will also be able to produce and edit content in The Post’s uniquely irreverent tone of voice, at high speed. The role requires a confident editorial leader, who will manage writers across multiple verticals including consumer lifestyle, science, tech, and viral trends. It reports to the Lifestyle Editor. Note: the shift for this role is Tuesday-Saturday. Responsibilities: ● Generating an endless font of innovative and agenda-setting daily trending and exclusive ideas. ● Assigning and editing trending daily stories, at high speed. ● Creating a short and long term strategy for the lifestyle news department, leveraging audience insights platforms, to meet the department’s goals. ● Overseeing the production of a number of daily stories — from writing headlines in the Post’s signature wit to ensuring SEO best practices to coordinating photo shoots and imagery. ● Constantly analyzing web traffic and referral metrics to drive audience engagement and traffic. ● Monitoring the news to look for opportunities to add depth to our headlines through original reporting, first-person perspectives and expert explainers. ● Managing the lifestyle news reporters and editors on the team. ● Coordinating closely with other departments such as photo, video, and audience development. Requirements: ● At least 5 years of editing experience in a news or fast moving magazine environment, preferably in a lifestyle or culture department. ● Excellent news judgement and the sharpest editing and writing prowess. ● Your finger on the pulse of the topics and trends of interest to the Post audience. ● Proven understanding of what makes a story successful across digital platforms - from headlines to visuals and optimization. ● Proficiency in WordPress or similar CMS. ● Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple stories, writers, and deadlines simultaneously. ● Comfortable making fast, decisive editorial calls in a breaking news environment. ● Proven team leader who is skilled at managing and developing writers and can work across departments including visuals, social, and audience development. ● Expertise with analytics tools and performance metrics to help guide coverage and strategy. ● A deep understanding of referral traffic, particularly, social, search and Discover. ● Proven experience in driving and retaining audiences, with deeper, engagement-focused content. Note: This role will be expected to report into the office 5 days per week. job.title: Manager of Commerce Partnerships
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post delivers the best in news, sports, entertainment and pop culture with wit, irreverence, and authority. Over the past 225+ years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. We are looking for a versatile Manager of Commerce Partnerships with a passion for affiliate marketing and digital sales to join our team! The ideal candidate must have a strong understanding of the digital landscape and the ability to identify revenue opportunities, build and maintain an active sales pipeline and close business at volume. Reporting into the Senior Director of Commerce Partnerships, this role will center around prospecting new opportunities, executing effective campaigns, and managing client relations for the development of long-term partnerships. Our team thrives in being analytical, detail-oriented, and able to coordinate and deliver projects with timely turnaround for the success of our clients and the business revenue initiatives of the company. Responsibilities: ● Build a book of accounts for long-term and repeat business, with a core focus on beauty and lifestyle categories. ● Negotiate competitive commission rates and explore monetization models best suited for different types of partnerships. Coordinate internally with cross-functional teams, including but not limited to Editorial, Ad Operations, Audience Development, Commerce, and Data to meet and execute on campaign objectives. ● Sell content and media campaigns across the New York Post’s suite of properties and capabilities. ● Work closely with our commerce content team to maximize revenue opportunities. ● Develop client relationships through continued communication and strategic optimization. ● Aim to deliver and exceed all quarterly budget goals. ● Respond to inbound opportunities and engage in proactive outreach. ● Be an active participant in strategic planning and brainstorming. ● Manage timelines and delivery of flat fee commerce campaigns. ● Assist in IO and media plan creation. ● Pull research and analyze data to guide sound business decisions. Requirements: ● 3-5 years of relevant experience. ● Strong understanding of affiliate marketing principles, strategies, and best practices. ● Exceptional communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills. ● Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data and derive actionable insights. ● Proficiency in using affiliate marketing platforms and analytics tools (e.g., CJ, Impact, Rakuten, Google Analytics, Looker, etc). ● Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and manage multiple priorities effectively. ● Detail-oriented with a focus on delivering high-quality results and exceeding client expectations. ● Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think strategically. ● Collaborative team player with a positive attitude and a passion for client success. job.title: News Reporter (Part-Time), The California Post
job.description: Job Description : We are looking for Part-Time News Reporters (~24 hours per week ) to join the California Post team. Reporting to the Deputy News Editor, the General Assignment News Reporter will have a focus on breaking exclusive stories and covering major events unfolding in Los Angeles and beyond. From delivering exclusive, engaging, agenda setting stories to covering wildfires, celebrity scandals, local politics, crime, courts and viral moments, this reporter will be on the front line of our coverage in one of the country’s most dynamic and newsworthy cities. Application Instructions: Applicants should submit a cover letter for consideration. Responsibilities: Deliver exclusive stories and cover breaking news across Los Angeles that drives engagement and audience for the California Post. Write fast, clean, and compelling copy that aligns with the Post’s distinctive voice and style Spot stories that resonate nationally, especially ones with viral or exclusive potential Develop sources across city agencies, emergency services, and local communities to get the inside track on stories Monitor court filings, public records, and social media for scoops and trending topics Collaborate with editors and fellow reporters to ensure comprehensive and coordinated coverage File updates in real time and across multiple platforms, including web, social, mobile, and video Uphold the highest journalistic standards of accuracy, fairness, and integrity Requirements: 1-3 years of experience reporting for a fast-paced digital or print newsroom Excellent news judgment and the ability to identify compelling angles others may miss High level of self-motivation, commitment to teamwork and ability to win in a competitive environment Proven ability to report and write on deadline while juggling multiple stories at once Experience covering major metro areas, ideally including public safety, politics, or general assignment Proven experience with WordPress of similar CMS highly preferred Strong sourcing skills and a relentless approach to newsgathering Proficiency in social media and SEO best practices Familiarity with court and public records; ability to navigate legal documents a plus A competitive drive to be first and best on big stories Strong writing and reporting skills are the core of this role On-camera experience is strongly preferred, as we’re looking for reporters who are comfortable discussing and presenting their stories on video to help extend our journalism across digital and social platforms A strong social media presence or following is a plus Spanish or other language fluency is a plus Note: This role will be expected to be onsite in our Century City office. job.title: Page Six Column Intern, Fall 2026 (10 weeks, 24 hours a week)
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 224 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. The New York Post Internship Program offers a dynamic, hands-on experience designed to give interns exposure to real world work within the media and news industry. Our interns are highly valued team members who work on meaningful projects that directly impact our business. Throughout the program, interns participate in career building masterclasses that support their professional growth and have the opportunity to build lasting relationships with peers and key leaders in the company. Build your skills, grow your network, and get an inside look at life behind the headlines. Page Six, which originally started as a gossip column on the sixth page of the New York Post, has since grown into a leading online digital brand. Focused on celebrity news, pop culture, and entertainment, Page Six now reaches millions of readers daily with exclusive stories, breaking news, and in-depth features. It has maintained its distinct voice while adapting to the digital landscape, becoming a go-to source for all things entertainment and continuing The Post’s legacy of bold, irreverent reporting. We are looking for a talented Page Six Column Intern (24 hrs/week) to join the PageSix team. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the world of celebrity news, pop culture, and entertainment. We're looking for a passionate, creative intern who’s obsessed with celebrities and eager to contribute to exciting journalism. If you're full of ideas, have a love for breaking stories, and are ready to get your hands dirty in the fast-paced media world, we want to hear from you. Note: This internship is scheduled to run from September 14, 2026 - November 20, 2026 . Open to current juniors and seniors pursuing a BA, MA students, and recent graduates who completed their degree within the past year. Note: This position requires in-office attendance at our Midtown Manhattan office. What You’ll Do: Collaborate with the PageSix team to brainstorm and pitch ideas for breaking news, features, and photo galleries. Assist with administrative tasks such as transcribing and research to support reporters. Write engaging stories covering all things pop culture, from celebrity news to entertainment trends. Help track and follow trending topics in the celebrity world to stay ahead of the curve. What We’re Looking For: Strong news judgment with the ability to identify and prioritize important stories. Excellent writing skills and the ability to craft compelling, engaging content. Self-starter who is able to work independently and take initiative. A genuine passion for celebrity culture, entertainment, and pop culture. Highly attuned to trending topics and emerging stories in the world of entertainment. As the go-to destination for breaking stories, exclusive scoops, and viral moments, Page Six has grown far beyond its print roots to become a dynamic, multi-platform brand that reaches millions of readers daily across web, social, and video. Page Six is looking for a bold, sharp, and pop culture-obsessed Reporter (Tues-Sat) who lives and breathes celebrity news. This is your chance to join the authority in entertainment gossip and help drive the conversations that everyone will be talking about tomorrow. You’ll pitch and write buzzy, can’t-miss stories daily with speed, accuracy, and unmistakable voice. We want someone who’s always one step ahead—plugged into social media trends, fluent in fan culture, and relentless in uncovering those juicy, under-the-radar scoops that make Page Six sizzle. If you thrive in a fast-paced newsroom, know your way around SEO and analytics, and can spot a viral moment before it breaks, we want to hear from you. Let’s make headlines. Note: The schedule for this role is Tuesday-Saturday 10am-6pm EST. job.title: Page Six Video Lead Editor
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture, Fashion and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 224 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. The Page Six video team is seeking a Lead Video Editor who will help us make existing series and compelling, shareable videos about celebrities, and fashion - subjects that are the mainstay of the nation’s most iconic gossip column. You should love celebrity journalism and possess deep knowledge about the latest celebrity gossip, trends, feuds, and hookups. You should live and breathe celebrity lifestyle, fashion and social media, with your fingers on the pulse. You’ll work in an extremely fast-paced environment enabling producers to hit production targets and goals. You’ll be the lead editor for the most important Page Six video series, both the audience favorites and the branded content as well. You’ll help create sizzles and other marketing assets as needed. You’ll supervise the rest of the editors, giving them creative notes, video editing workflow best practices, troubleshooting problems and overall quality control. You’ll coordinate media backups with our production management team. And work with our team and creative director to have graphic guidelines as well as create custom graphics and thumbnails to help click through rates. You must edit fast and with a flourish. Expertise with key products in Adobe Creative Suite (Premiere, Photoshop, After Effects) as well as Adobe graphic templates. You’ll edit videos for digital platforms using a mix of original footage, stock footage and social media content. Along with editing digitally-native video, you will help generate our content, pitching video ideas daily and contributing to the team brainstorming. We seek a candidate who is excited about new types of multimedia storytelling and has a track record of creating digital video in a fast-paced news organization. Must be aware of the latest formats and trends in digital video as a distinct form of content versus television. This is a fast-paced job that requires a love of all things celebrity, a strong editorial sense and the ability to stay organized while multitasking. Like us, you believe news doesn’t have to be boring and you appreciate the odd and unconventional stories as well as important ones. This is an opportunity to work with an iconic media brand as it experiences exponential digital growth. New York Post and Page Six videos have received more than a billion views in the past few years. Responsibilities: ● Lead the editing and post-production of high-priority Page Six video series, branded content, and celebrity-focused digital features optimized for social and web platforms. ● Supervise and mentor video editors by providing creative direction, workflow guidance, troubleshooting support, and overall quality control in a fast-paced newsroom environment. ● Edit compelling, digitally native videos using original footage, stock assets, and social media content while maintaining Page Six’s signature voice, tone, and style. ● Collaborate with producers, creative leadership, and production management to develop graphics packages, thumbnails, sizzle reels, and promotional assets that drive audience engagement and click-through rates. ● Pitch timely celebrity, fashion, and entertainment video concepts daily, contributing innovative storytelling ideas aligned with trending topics and audience interests. ● Manage multiple projects simultaneously under tight deadlines, ensuring efficient turnaround, media organization, backups, and adherence to production schedules. ● Apply advanced post-production techniques including color correction, audio mixing, multi-cam editing, and vertical video formatting using Adobe Creative Suite tools such as Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Photoshop. The ideal candidate will have: ● 5-10 years experience editing celebrity videos for digital outlets ● Expertise with Adobe Creative Suite, specifically Premiere ● Knowledge of studio and control room operations ● Ability to color correct and mix audio. ● Ability to create vertical videos for various social platforms ● Be able to work very quickly under pressure ● Pitch video ideas daily and contribute to team brainstorming. ● Experience with multicam editing ● Motion graphics experience a plus as is simple animation, but not necessary ● Ability to select and use music to match the tone and style of the story ● Must be organized, work well in a fast-paced environment and be a team-player. ● Can-do attitude is key: someone who believes news doesn’t have to be boring and who appreciates the odd and unconventional stories as well as important ones. ● Open to working evenings and weekends, on rare cases if required ● Experience working autonomously in a fast-paced newsroom environment on weekly deadlines Note: This role is expected to be on-site in the New York metro area five days per week. job.title: Page Six West Coast News Editor, Exclusives
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post delivers news, sports, pop culture and entertainment with unmatched speed, attitude and authority, reaching more than 90 million unique viewers each month. With a 225 year legacy and a fast moving digital first newsroom, the Post operates across print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce, and continues to define the city’s most talked about stories. Page Six is one of the most iconic brands in entertainment and pop culture journalism, and we’re looking for a strategic, experienced editorial leader to take it to the next level on the West Coast. Reporting into the News Editor, Exclusives, with a dotted line to the News Editor, California Post, the Page SIx West Coast News Editor, Exclusives will lead Page Six’s enterprise operation on the West Coast and differentiate Page Six and the California Post in an increasingly crowded landscape. This role is responsible for building and guiding a team of reporters focused on original, agenda-setting stories, identifying exclusive beats, and cultivating sources that allow Page Six to break the news, not chase it. This is a senior, strategic role that oversees stories from ideation to execution. The ideal candidate understands that exclusives are integral to the continued growth and evolution of Page Six as a business. We need someone with a proven track record of delivering fast-paced stories on the West Coast while adhering to the highest journalistic standards of sourcing and accuracy. They need a network of industry contacts and a deep understanding of California and what Angelinos really care about in the Entertainment space. Responsibilities: Lead and manage a team of West Coast reporters focused on identifying, developing, and executing exclusive, agenda-setting stories that distinguish Page Six and the California Post from their competitors, drive sustained impact and audience growth. Maintaining existing and developing new industry contacts. Attend daily Page Six Exclusives and California Post meetings to identify source opportunities, troubleshoot reporting challenges, and refine news strategy in real time. Work closely with New York and California newsrooms to drive original reporting and break exclusives. Ensure exclusive story efforts are tightly aligned with broader news priorities and coverage plans of Page Six and the California Post. Contribute to the broader growth of Page Six and the California Post by increasing editorial authority and reputation. The ideal candidate will have: A minimum of 7 years professional experience in entertainment journalism, with significant success breaking news and developing sources. Strong experience leading teams during breaking news situations and advancing stories through diverse sourcing and follow-up reporting. A strong understanding of journalistic ethics and the legal standards governing reporting, including source protection, libel and defamation, and responsible handling of sensitive stories. Exceptional news judgment with a deep knowledge of the key players in the entertainment industry on the West Coast. Extensive experience breaking timely and accurate court and legal updates as well as a thorough knowledge of requesting police reports, mug shots, body-camera footage, court filings, and financial, business and real estate records to support exclusive reporting. A leadership style that sets a high bar for performance and accountability, leads by example, and fosters an environment where reporters are supported, challenged, and consistently producing standout work. Strong editing and fact-checking skills, with meticulous attention to detail under tight deadlines. An extensive contacts book. The ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, high-pressure newsroom environment. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Consistent delivery of agenda-setting exclusives that lead coverage across the entertainment news cycle and help differentiate Page Six and the California Post from their competitors. A measurable contribution to Page Six’s brand growth, audience engagement, and reputation as a market leader in entertainment news. Contribution to significant audience growth in The Californian market. Note: This role will be expected to report into our California office 5 days per week (subject to change depending on business needs). job.title: Prepress Technician

Manage time effectively to meet deadlines, prioritizing complex or high-scrutiny imagery as needed. Strong attention to detail with the ability to monitor pages for technical and quality errors under deadline pressure. Experience with pagination systems (Methode experience preferred), including programming, troubleshooting, and user support/training. Proficiency in image correction and color separation for print, including adjusting contrast, brightness, and color for newsprint reproduction. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with editorial staff and photo editors. job.title: PT Editor
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture, Fashion and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 224 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce. The NY Post is looking for an experienced editor for a part-time role with the Sunday staff. The editor is expected to be a line and assignment editor who possesses fine attention to detail, critical thinking skills, and who can also aggressively transform breaking copy on deadline to sing in The Post's unique tabloid voice. The editor should be able to mine, assign and edit an array of stories -- impactful, quirky, scandalous, etc. -- on immediate deadline for our website, and also for the Sunday print edition. The editor must be able to give clear direction to our team of award-winning field reporters and in-office journos. The Sunday team breaks local, national and international news, investigates government corruption, crushes hypocrisy wherever we find it, mines the world for the quirky and the funny, and delivers award-winning, long- and short-form journalism in the boldest tabloid voice. The NY Post is the nation’s 5th-largest U.S. newspaper by circulation and its website routinely generates tens of millions of pageviews every weekend. The ability to handle anything from a breaking brief to a sprawling news feature, in a wide range of subjects, is needed. And you’ll even get to spitball with the rest of us on our world-famous Page 1 headlines. Qualifications: ● Bachelor’s degree or higher ● A minimum of 5 years of editing in a busy newsroom ● Comfortable editing/re-writing both breaking news and long-form stories in lively tabloid prose for web and print ● A keen understanding of the voice of the Post ● A knack for finding stories our readers crave ● A critical eye for facts and tone ● Broad knowledge base ● Willingness to collaborate and ability to communicate with a close-knit team of NYC’s best journalists Note: The New York Post adheres to a hybrid work model. As a part-time editor, you will work an 8-to-10-hour Saturday shift in the office, with the possibility of working additional hours on Thursday and Friday. At The New York Post we recognize that attracting the best talent is key to our strategy and success as a company. job.title: Senior Human Resources Manager, People Business Partner
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post is seeking a Senior Manager, People Business Partner based in New York City. This is an important role supporting leaders across the newsroom and commercial functions, helping execute strategies for a fast-moving, high-profile media organization. Reporting to the Human Resources Director, you will partner closely with leaders and employees to support organizational effectiveness, talent management, employee engagement, and culture initiatives. This role requires strong judgment, adaptability, and the ability to operate effectively in a performance-driven, deadline-oriented environment. You will bring a practical, solutions-focused mindset and collaborate closely with HR colleagues and corporate partners to ensure alignment, consistency, and application of best practices. WHAT YOU’LL DO Partner with department leaders and employees to align people strategies with the New York Post’s editorial, commercial, and digital priorities. Support organizational design efforts, workforce planning, and change initiatives in collaboration with senior HR leadership. Provide guidance on employee engagement, performance management, talent development, and career progression in fast-paced teams. Manage and resolve employee relations matters, including investigations, performance concerns, and workplace conflict, with sound judgment and discretion. Leverage data and workforce insights to inform decision-making and recommend practical solutions. Promote transparent communication and contribute to a culture of accountability, inclusion, and trust. Support innovation and process improvements, including adoption of AI tools where appropriate, to enhance team effectiveness. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR An experienced and credible HR professional who understands business priorities and delivers practical, actionable solutions. Strong relationship-builder who can influence and coach managers with confidence. Comfortable navigating ambiguity while escalating appropriately when needed. Clear, direct communicator with strong interpersonal skills. Proactive and resilient, with the ability to manage competing priorities. Collaborative team player who contributes to a culture of performance and shared success. WHAT YOU HAVE 6+ years of progressive HR experience, including 3+ years in an HR Business Partner or equivalent client-facing role. Bachelor’s degree in HR, business, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience). Experience supporting fast-paced teams, including commercial, sales, or editorial/creative environments. Strong foundation in employee relations, investigations, and performance management. Working knowledge of employment laws and HR best practices. Demonstrated ability to balance business partnership with employee advocacy. Experience operating within a matrixed or complex organization preferred. Strong coaching, influencing, and problem-solving skills. Data-informed mindset with experience using metrics to guide action. Ability to manage sensitive situations with professionalism and discretion. Willingness to work on-site in midtown Manhattan in alignment with a hybrid model. Note: This role is based in our Midtown Manhattan office and follows a hybrid work schedule. job.title: Senior Software Engineering Manager
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post is one of America’s most iconic and recognizable news brands — delivering bold headlines, unforgettable scoops, and sharp commentary since 1801. With a legacy built on fearless j ournalism and a distinctly New York attitude, The Post has evolved far beyond its print roots to become a modern media powerhouse. Today, the New York Post Digital Network is one of the most influential voices in the industry, reaching over 80 million unique users each month across our expansive, ever-growing portfolio. Anchored by NYPost.com, PageSix.com, and Decider.com, our digital brands deliver must-read breaking news, sports, entertainment, pop culture, and lifestyle coverage with the same wit, edge, and energy that define The Post. With innovation at our core, we’ve built a true multi-platform ecosystem — spanning web, mobile apps, video, audio, social, print, TV, and commerce. From viral headlines and exclusive stories to original series, podcasts, and live events, we’re engaging audiences where they are — and always on the pulse of what’s next. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineering Manager to join our technology team and lead the systems that power The Post’s digital future. This is a hands-on engineering role with core responsibilities around infrastructure services, data pipelines, personalization systems, consumer AI, internal AI tooling, and custom APIs across AWS and GCP projects. You are a hands-on technical leader who builds robust high-performance services for websites. You will own the plumbing that enables our newsroom, data science, marketing, and product teams to deliver cutting-edge digital experiences at scale. You’ll work alongside technology leadership in a fast-paced newsroom. You will partner with editorial leaders, share architectural solutions with other business units in the US, UK, and Australia, and direct your engineering team with experienced tactics and thoughtful strategy. Please Note: Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis. Sponsorship, including employment visa sponsorship or transfer, is not available for this position now or in the future. Key Responsibilities: Manage and support a small team of high-achieving agile software and data engineers. Design, build, and operate cloud-based APIs supporting specialized needs of our consumer websites, native mobile apps. Work daily with compute services, query services, storage services, and big data services with technologies like Vertex AI, Lambdas, DynamoDB, Cloud Functions, S3, Kubernetes, Glue, and BigQuery. Be able to personally troubleshoot an issue from Javascript in a browser down through DNS, networking, applications, containers and operating systems or serverless services, and into dependent service tiers. Own data ingestion pipelines for real-time and batch processing of large-scale content and event data. Understand how to implement and scale custom APIs to support editorial workflows, AI, personalization, analytics, and user-facing applications. Own the team’s codebases, pull requests, testing, maintenance and release process. Partner with product, editorial, and data science teams to deliver infrastructure and services that meet business needs. Monitor, optimize, and improve the reliability, security, and cost efficiency of cloud-based systems. Communicate and present a vision for both technical and non-technical audiences. Organize architecture discussions. Run and/or supervise agile sprint ceremonies. Qualifications: Must-Haves MS or BS in computer science, or related field. 10+ years of professional software engineering experience. 5+ years experience leading engineering teams. Agile best practices. Proficiency in modern programming languages and frameworks such as Python, Node.js, or Go. Solid familiarity of common AWS and/or GCP services . Robust experience with REST and GraphQL APIs, authentication/authorization, and API best practices. Firm grasp of the tools of the trade including AI tools, IDEs, Git, JIRA, and agile methodologies. Comfort with code reviews, unit tests, QA and UAT processes, and knowledge of end-to-end testing frameworks. Strong troubleshooting skills Attention to detail, thoroughness, a proactive approach to problem-solving, and a comfort in diving in and learning things from scratch. Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Great-to-Have Experience Familiarity with content-management systems, media, news, publishing, video technology, ad technology, or other high-traffic consumer-facing industries. Hands-on experience with generative-AI models, LLM prompting, and/or machine learning. Personalization and recommendation systems. Experience building and deploying data pipelines (e.g., Airflow, Dataflow, Glue, or similar tools) Comfort with Linux administration, shell scripting, ssh, crontabs, etc. Experience with monitoring, logging, dashboard, and alarming tools (e.g., CloudWatch, Datadog, Splunk, etc.) Knowledge of data warehouse technologies (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.) Understanding of CI/CD workflows and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes a plus) Note: The New York Post follows a hybrid work model. This position would be expected to be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week (subject to change). job.title: Washington Correspondent
job.description: Job Description : The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture, and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence, and authority, averaging 90 million unique monthly viewers. Over the past 225 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television, and commerce. Politics is core to who we are — and nobody covers it like The Post. We break big stories, stir the pot, and shine a light on what’s really going on in the nation’s capital. From policy drama and power grabs to scandals and backstabbing, we’re looking for someone who gets the whole DC circus and can help lead the way in breaking news. The New York Post is seeking an enterprising DC-based Washington Correspondent to join our growing DC team and cover the fast-moving world of Washington politics. This reporter will break exclusive stories, expose what’s happening behind the scenes in government, and bring readers sharp, authoritative coverage of how decisions in the capital shape the nation. Land interviews with power brokers in DC politics Cover legislative battles, policy shifts, elections, and key political figures. Break exclusive stories and find fresh angles on widely covered issues that others will chase Build and maintain a strong network of sources, from lawmakers and lobbyists to administration and campaign officials. Stay on top of political developments in real time and file timely, accurate copy. Use public records, FOIA requests, and social media to surface and verify stories. Work closely with editors and colleagues to produce fast, engaging coverage across digital and social platforms. ​ Requirements: Minimum seven years of newsroom reporting experience, with a focus on DC or political coverage. Experience writing about the White House and Congress and building sources within the Trump administration Proven ability to break news, cultivate sources, and deliver original, high-impact reporting Strong editorial judgment and writing skills under tight deadlines. job.title: Assistant Chief Engineer
job.description: FOX4 (WDAF-TV) is looking for a hands-on broadcast engineer to work alongside the Chief Engineer keeping our television plant on the air, and to help build what comes next. This is a television engineering job first. Our SDI plant, control rooms, and live newscasts are the product, and they have to work every single day. At the same time, the station is expanding into connected TV and streaming delivery, and whoever takes this role will have a real hand in shaping that side of the operation as it grows. We would rather hire someone who can trace a signal, read a rack, and stay steady during a live show, and then teach them the rest. Core Responsibilities Broadcast and Production Systems Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain studio, control room, and master control systems Trace and manage signal flow across a large SDI plant, including routing, conversion, monitoring, and audio distribution Support live news production, including Ross OverDrive automation, production switchers, graphics systems, and audio consoles Respond quickly and calmly when something breaks on the air Create and maintain clear documentation of how systems are wired and how they are repaired Information Technology and Networking Keep broadcast-attached servers, workstations, shared storage, and backups running in coordination with corporate IT Maintain switches, VLANs, and the networks our production and newsroom systems depend on Apply updates and follow the cybersecurity practices set by Nexstar corporate IT Please note: this is broadcast IT, not a help desk or enterprise system administration role. Corporate IT owns the enterprise side. What we need here is someone who understands how the network serves the plant. Streaming and Connected TV Help support and expand our connected TV and streaming encoding, distribution, and monitoring Work with the Chief Engineer to plan how new delivery paths fit alongside existing linear infrastructure Bring ideas about how the plant should evolve, not just keep the lights on No prior CTV or streaming experience is required. Curiosity and a willingness to learn matter more. Facilities and Operations Assist with generator, UPS, HVAC, power, and physical security systems Support readiness during severe weather and power events Assist with transmitter and tower site maintenance under the direction of the Chief Engineer Help maintain a safe, efficient, and reliable technical environment Project and Vendor Management Research and evaluate new technology for integration into station operations Request quotes, coordinate vendors and contractors, and oversee project timelines Track capital and special projects through planning, installation, and documentation Maintain accurate technical inventories and service records Leadership and Collaboration Serve as the senior technical contact when the Chief Engineer is off site or unavailable Provide practical guidance to maintenance engineers and operations staff Communicate clearly with newsroom, production, and corporate personnel Maintain a calm, professional demeanor under pressure and during live operations Qualifications What We Require: Hands-on broadcast or live production technical experience. You have personally traced signal, terminated cable, read a rack, and used test gear Three or more years in broadcast engineering, television technical operations, or live production technology Working comfort with Windows systems and basic networking, enough to be useful rather than expert level Composure during live television, and the judgment to know what to fix first Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work safely in studios, racks, catwalks, and rooftop environments Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record Willingness to be on call and respond after hours during severe weather and power events Preferred but Not Required Experience with Ross Carbonite, or comparable production switchers Windows Server and Active Directory familiarity SBE certification or an FCC General Radiotelephone License An associate or bachelor’s degree in engineering, information technology, or a related field. Equivalent hands-on experience carries the same weight The Right Fit This position is designed for a well-rounded engineer who thrives at the intersection of broadcast and IT. You will be empowered to maintain, improve, and innovate across all technical systems while providing vital support to a fast-paced, live news environment. The ideal candidate is a steady hand, a creative problem solver, and a trusted partner ready to help lead one of Kansas City’s most dynamic media operations.

job.title: Broadcast Maintenance Engineer
job.description: Nexstar Media Chicago is a powerhouse in linear TV and streaming, operating 5 studios, 3 control rooms, and 5 streaming studios producing live content around the clock. NewsNation reaches 75 million households nationwide, and WGN-TV is Chicago’s #1 local station. Our brands also include Antenna TV and Rewind TV. We’re seeking a full-time Broadcast Maintenance Engineer with strong IT skills to join our engineering team. You’ll provide daily maintenance and technical operational support for a large, complex broadcast facility, ensuring all broadcast systems, technology, and live day-of-air programs maintain on-air reliability across traditional and digital platforms. This position requires a combination of maintenance, I.T. and project management/system engineering skills. Key Responsibilities Maintain and troubleshoot broadcast and IT systems, including studio/control room automation, master control, ENPS newsroom, cameras, audio gear, and streaming encoders. Configure and troubleshoot IP networking for servers and broadcast equipment. Diagnose signal flow and data flow issues; interpret schematics and system drawings. Strong hands-on problem-solving skills with broadcast-related equipment and systems. Support remote feed technologies (Dejero, TVU, Haivision) and streaming workflows. Support and assist studio operations within a live production environment. Collaborate with engineering team to meet deadlines and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment. Collaborate with production and operations team to execute technical solutions that meet production needs in a timely fashion. Desired Skills & Experience Strong knowledge of IP networking (LAN/VLAN/WAN/VPN), Active Directory, Windows/Linux platforms. Proficiency with broadcast production systems and software, including audio consoles, intercom systems, video switchers, wireless audio, and test and measurement equipment. Familiarity with broadcast systems: Ross Xpression/Tessera, LED videowalls, Dante audio, satellite transmission. Ability to use network tools (ping, traceroute) and common test equipment (signal generators, scopes). Understanding of video compression, resolutions (e.g., 1080i) and bandwidth requirements. Ability to read and understand technical system signal flow diagrams for studio facilities. Strong hands-on problem-solving skills with broadcast-related equipment and systems. Excellent written and communication skills, with the ability to diplomatically engage with colleagues across various departments. Proficiency in newsroom and production environments, especially software driven. Manage projects, design systems, and assist with system integration and commissioning. Requirements: Five (5) years' experience as an IT technician or maintenance engineer in a media facility is desired. An Associate or Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline is a plus. Ability to lift 50 lbs. Knowledge of common business software applications. This position will require shift work which may include nights, weekends, and holidays, along with overtime as situations will sometimes require. This position requires membership in IBEW 1220. #LI-Onsite Compensation: $27.87 to $46.68 per hour - commensurate with applicant's experience and skill level Benefits: Our comprehensive benefits package includes, but not limited to, medical (with multiple plan options), dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, Paid Parental leave, life insurance and more.
